title: Machine learning classifies painful versus painless diabetic peripheral neuropathy
summary: Random forest, adaptive regression splines and naive Bayes models were trained on harmonised cohorts (N = 935, cross-validated) and externally validated on a population-based cohort (N = 295). Random forest (MCC 0.28, AUPRC 0.76) and adaptive regression splines (MCC 0.29, AUPRC 0.77) performed best. Top predictors included EQ5D index, personality dimensions, HbA1c, depression and anxiety scores, age and BMI. Cohorts are cross-sectional and the MCC values are modest; associations are not causal.
ai_technology: Random forest, adaptive regression splines and naive Bayes classifiers

evidence.tested: Cross-validation in N = 935 and external validation in an independent population-based cohort (N = 295).
evidence.unknown: Causal role of the predictors and prospective use; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Classifies painful versus painless DPN and ranks predictors by importance.
